findings.title: Greeting name invariant is implemented in a service with no domain value object boundary

findings.title: REST errors use a custom ErrorResponse instead of ProblemDetail/ResponseEntityExceptionHandler
findings.description: The project standard requires Spring Boot error responses to use ProblemDetail via @ControllerAdvice and ResponseEntityExceptionHandler. GlobalExceptionHandler is a @RestControllerAdvice that returns a custom ErrorResponse through ResponseEntity, so validation errors do not follow the required RFC 9457-style contract and framework exceptions will not be centrally normalized through ResponseEntityExceptionHandler.

findings.suggestedFix: Change the handler to extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler and return ProblemDetail for REST errors, or override the relevant ResponseEntityExceptionHandler methods so validation, binding, and framework errors share the same sanitized contract.

findings.title: Stacktrace suppression is not explicitly configured

findings.title: Public service parameter null contract is not explicit
findings.description: `GreetingService.greet(String name)` has public behavior for null input, as covered by the test, but the parameter has no nullability or validation annotation. The null-safety checklist requires ambiguous parameters and return types to be annotated where ambiguity exists.

findings.description: The project targets Java 21 and uses Spring Boot, but application.yml does not configure `spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true`. Without this setting, Spring MVC request handling continues to use platform threads by default, so the migration does not benefit from Java 21 virtual-thread scalability. The current code is small and synchronous, so this is an adoption/configuration gap rather than an immediate deadlock or data-race risk.

findings.suggestedFix:
Add:

spring:
  threads:
    virtual:

  application:
    name: sample-java-code

Then run the Spring MVC tests and a smoke test to confirm request handling remains correct.

findings.title: Global exception handler does not return ProblemDetail or cover unhandled exceptions
findings.description: The @RestControllerAdvice only handles validation-related exceptions and returns a custom ErrorResponse. The review standard requires RFC 7807 ProblemDetail responses and a catch-all handler for unexpected exceptions so clients receive a sanitized 500 response with a consistent error shape. Runtime failures outside validation currently fall through to Spring Boot's default error handling instead of the application's reviewed error contract.
findings.evidence: Handlers exist only for MethodArgumentNotValidException, HandlerMethodValidationException, and ConstraintViolationException, and badRequest() returns ResponseEntity<ErrorResponse> rather than ProblemDetail.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace ErrorResponse with ProblemDetail-based handlers and add @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) that logs the exception server-side and returns a sanitized 500 ProblemDetail. Add domain-specific handlers as custom exceptions are introduced.

findings.title: No correlation ID filter or MDC propagation is implemented
findings.description: Requests are not assigned or propagated with X-Correlation-Id, and no MDC value is set or cleared. This prevents correlating logs for a single request during incident triage and violates the review requirement for correlation ID consistency.
findings.evidence: Search found no references to MDC, X-Correlation-Id, Filter, or HandlerInterceptor implementation in the target application files.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a OncePerRequestFilter that reads or generates X-Correlation-Id, calls MDC.put("correlationId", value), sets the response header, invokes the filter chain, and clears MDC in finally. Include correlationId in the log pattern or JSON encoder fields.

findings.title: Production JSON logging configuration is missing
findings.description: The project has no logback-spring.xml and does not include logstash-logback-encoder, so logs are not configured for structured JSON output with correlation fields. This weakens log searchability and breaks the review standard for production structured logging.
findings.evidence: Dependencies include validation, web, and test only; no logstash-logback-encoder dependency is present. File discovery also found no logback-spring.xml.
findings.suggestedFix: Add net.logstash.logback:logstash-logback-encoder and a logback-spring.xml that emits JSON logs including timestamp, level, logger, message, exception, spring.application.name, and MDC correlationId.

findings.title: Spring Boot Actuator is not configured
findings.description: The project lacks spring-boot-starter-actuator and management endpoint configuration. The review standard requires Actuator health/metrics availability for production observability.

findings.suggestedFix: Add spring-boot-starter-actuator and configure management endpoints intentionally, for example exposing health and metrics with appropriate production access controls.

findings.title: No Spring Security dependency or SecurityFilterChain is configured
findings.description: The application has Spring Web but no Spring Security starter, and no SecurityFilterChain/HttpSecurity configuration was found. Under the supplied review standard, this means request authorization, authentication provider/JWT filter configuration, CSRF/session policy, and security headers are all absent, leaving every endpoint public by framework default.
findings.evidence: Dependencies include spring-boot-starter-validation, spring-boot-starter-web, and spring-boot-starter-test only. Repository search found no SecurityFilterChain or HttpSecurity usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add spring-boot-starter-security and a @Configuration class defining SecurityFilterChain in the required order: CORS if needed, CSRF policy, sessionManagement, authorizeHttpRequests, authentication provider/JWT/basic auth, and headers. Permit only intentional public endpoints such as /api/health.

findings.title: Stack trace exposure setting is not explicitly disabled
findings.description: application.yml does not set server.error.include-stacktrace: never, and there is no production profile file setting it either. The review standard requires this to be explicit to prevent stack traces from being exposed through error responses if defaults or profiles change.
findings.evidence: The file only configures server.port and spring.application.name.
findings.suggestedFix: Add server.error.include-stacktrace: never to common and production configuration, for example under server: error: include-stacktrace: never.

findings.title: Profile-based configuration separation is missing
findings.description: Only application.yml exists. There is no application-dev.yml or application-prod.yml to separate local settings from production hardening such as production log levels, stacktrace policy, SQL visibility, and HTTPS/proxy assumptions.
findings.evidence: src/main/resources contains only application.yml.
findings.suggestedFix: Create profile-specific configuration files. Keep common safe defaults in application.yml, development-only settings in application-dev.yml, and production settings such as logging.level.root: WARN and server.error.include-stacktrace: never in application-prod.yml.

findings.title: Structured/profile-specific Logback configuration is absent
findings.description: No logback-spring.xml was found, so profile-specific logging appenders and production-oriented structured logging are not configured in the target project.
findings.evidence: Resource file listing showed only src/main/resources/application.yml.
findings.suggestedFix: Add logback-spring.xml with dev and prod springProfile sections, production root level WARN, and a structured encoder if production log ingestion expects JSON.

findings.category: A01 Broken Access Control / Security Baseline
findings.title: No Spring Security dependency or default-deny SecurityFilterChain
findings.description: The application is a Spring Web API but the dependency set contains validation, web, and test only. There is no Spring Security dependency or SecurityFilterChain with an explicit permit list and `.anyRequest().authenticated()` fallback, so all current and future endpoints are public by Spring Boot default. Current endpoints are low-sensitivity health/greeting APIs, but this violates the supplied default-deny requirement and creates a high-risk expansion path for user/order/admin APIs.
findings.evidence: Dependencies include `spring-boot-starter-validation`, `spring-boot-starter-web`, and `spring-boot-starter-test`; no `spring-boot-starter-security` is present. `rg` found no `SecurityFilterChain` in the target source.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `spring-boot-starter-security` and a security configuration that explicitly permits only intended public endpoints, for example `/api/health`, then requires authentication for all others. Add role matchers for any future admin paths.

findings.category: Security Headers / A07 XSS Defense in Depth
findings.title: Security headers are not explicitly configured
findings.description: Because there is no security configuration and `application.yml` only sets the port and application name, the app does not explicitly enforce CSP, frame denial, referrer policy, permissions policy, HSTS, or server-header suppression required by the review standard. The current API returns JSON only, so practical XSS exposure is limited, but the missing headers weaken browser-side defense in depth and can become exploitable if UI/templates are added.
findings.evidence: `application.yml` contains only `server.port` and `spring.application.name`; no header hardening or `server.server-header` suppression is configured, and no Spring Security headers configuration exists in source.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure Spring Security headers: `contentTypeOptions`, `frameOptions().deny`, CSP such as `default-src 'self'`, HSTS for TLS deployments, strict referrer policy, and permissions policy. Set `server.server-header:` blank where supported.

findings.title: Public endpoints have no rate limiting or request-size/connection hardening
findings.description: `GET /api/greetings` and `POST /api/greetings` are public and perform request parsing plus validation, but there is no rate limiting, request body size limit, header size limit, or Tomcat timeout hardening in application configuration. Name length validation limits the business field to 40 characters, but it does not protect the HTTP parser or JSON body processing from request floods or oversized bodies.
findings.evidence: `application.yml` lacks `server.tomcat.connection-timeout`, request/header size settings, multipart/form limits, or any rate limiting configuration. Controller exposes public endpoints at `GreetingController.java:34`, `GreetingController.java:45`, and `GreetingController.java:57`.
findings.suggestedFix: Add rate limiting for public endpoints, especially POST, via a filter/gateway/Bucket4j-style mechanism. Configure bounded request sizes and timeouts appropriate for this API, such as max request/header size and Tomcat connection/keep-alive timeouts.

findings.title: Non-validation exception responses are not explicitly sanitized in application config
findings.description: The global exception handler sanitizes validation errors, but it does not define a generic sanitized response for unexpected exceptions, and `application.yml` does not explicitly pin `server.error.include-stacktrace=never`, `server.error.include-message=never`, or binding-error suppression. Spring Boot defaults are generally safe, but relying on defaults is weaker than an explicit production security posture and can regress through profile/config changes.
findings.evidence: Only `MethodArgumentNotValidException`, `HandlerMethodValidationException`, and `ConstraintViolationException` are handled. `application.yml` has no `server.error.*` hardening settings.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit `server.error.include-stacktrace: never`, `server.error.include-message: never`, and `server.error.include-binding-errors: never`. Consider a generic `@ExceptionHandler` that returns a sanitized RFC 7807/ProblemDetail response while logging server-side details without PII.

findings.title: Spring Boot parent version does not match required 3.2.x baseline
findings.description: The review standard requires `spring-boot-starter-parent` version `3.2.x`, but this POM uses `3.5.8`. This breaks the mandated BOM baseline and can change managed dependency versions across the project.

findings.title: Required observability dependency is missing for the web API module

findings.title: Maven source and reporting encoding properties are not defined

findings.suggestedFix: Add `<project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>` and `<project.reporting.outputEncoding>UTF-8</project.reporting.outputEncoding>` under `<properties>`.

findings.title: Controller test method names do not follow should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition

findings.suggestedFix: Rename methods, for example: should_returnUp_when_healthEndpointRequested, should_returnGreeting_when_nameProvidedAsQuery, should_returnValidationError_when_queryNameBlank.

findings.title: Service test method names do not follow should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition
findings.description: All three service test methods violate the required should_ExpectedResult_when_Condition naming convention. The names describe behavior, but they do not encode expected result and condition in the mandated format.

findings.suggestedFix: Rename methods, for example: should_normalizeRepeatedWhitespace_when_nameContainsExtraSpaces, should_throwIllegalArgumentException_when_nameBlank, should_throwIllegalArgumentException_when_nameNull.

findings.title: Service tests embed Act inside Assert and do not clearly separate AAA blocks
findings.description: The service tests directly call greetingService.greet(...) inside assertThat/assertThatThrownBy without explicit Arrange, Act, and Assert separation. The Act step is not isolated as a single method call, which violates the review agent's AAA requirement.
findings.evidence: Example: line 14 calls greetingService.greet(...) inside assertThat(...); lines 20 and 27 call greetingService.greet(...) inside assertThatThrownBy(...).
findings.suggestedFix: Use explicit blocks: arrange input, act with one call such as var result = greetingService.greet(input), then assert with AssertJ. For exception tests, assign ThrowingCallable act = () -> greetingService.greet(input); then assertThatThrownBy(act).

findings.title: Controller tests do not clearly separate Arrange, Act, and Assert
findings.description: Each MockMvc test chains perform(...) and andExpect(...) directly. This keeps the tests compact, but under the configured standard the Act and Assert phases are not clearly separated and there are no Arrange/Act/Assert comments or blank-block structure.
findings.evidence: Example: lines 33-35 perform the request and assertions in one chain; the same pattern appears in all five tests.
findings.suggestedFix: Store the result of mockMvc.perform(...) in a ResultActions variable under an Act block, then place all andExpect(...) calls in the Assert block, with clear // Arrange, // Act, // Assert comments or spacing.

findings.title: Existing coverage report shows public methods are untested

findings.title: Controller error-case tests are fewer than happy-path tests
findings.description: The controller suite has three successful-path tests and two error-path tests. The configured review standard requires error cases to be equal to or greater than happy paths. Missing cases include max-length validation failures and malformed/missing request body behavior.
findings.evidence: Happy paths: healthReturnsUp, greetByQueryReturnsGreeting, greetByBodyReturnsGreeting. Error paths: greetByQueryRejectsBlankName, greetByBodyRejectsBlankName.
findings.suggestedFix: Add controller error tests for query name > 40 chars, body name > 40 chars, missing body name, and malformed JSON or empty body as applicable.

findings.title: Tests do not use @DisplayName for human-readable specifications
findings.description: No test method has @DisplayName. The review standard expects @DisplayName usage for human-readable descriptions, with Japanese descriptions allowed.
findings.evidence: rg found @Test usages in both test classes but no @DisplayName imports or annotations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @DisplayName to each test, for example @DisplayName("Returns greeting when name is provided as query parameter").

findings.title: Validation boundary values for @Size(max = 40) are not tested
findings.description: The production API enforces @Size(max = 40) for query and body names, but the tests only cover blank names. Boundary values at exactly 40 characters and 41 characters are missing.
findings.evidence: GreetingController uses @Size(max = 40) on query name; GreetingRequest uses @Size(max = 40) on body name. Existing controller error tests only pass a single blank string.
findings.suggestedFix: Add tests such as should_returnGreeting_when_queryNameHasMaxLength and should_returnValidationError_when_queryNameExceedsMaxLength; repeat for JSON body. Consider @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource for invalid cases.

findings.title: Spring Boot Actuator liveness/readiness probes are missing
findings.description: The resilience standard requires `/actuator/health` and `/actuator/health/readiness`. The project only exposes a custom `/api/health` controller endpoint and does not include Actuator or management health probe configuration, so orchestrators cannot use standard liveness/readiness endpoints.
findings.evidence: `application.yml` only defines `server.port` and `spring.application.name`. `pom.xml` dependencies at lines 25-39 include validation, web, and test only; no `spring-boot-starter-actuator`. `GreetingController.java:34` exposes `/api/health`, which is not an Actuator readiness/liveness probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `spring-boot-starter-actuator` to `pom.xml` and configure health probes, for example: `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: health,info,metrics`, `management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled: true`, `management.health.livenessstate.enabled: true`, and `management.health.readinessstate.enabled: true`. Keep `/api/health` only as an optional smoke endpoint.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown is not configured
findings.description: The application does not configure Spring Boot graceful shutdown. During rolling restarts or pod termination, in-flight requests may be interrupted instead of being drained cleanly.
findings.evidence: No `server.shutdown: graceful` or `spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase` settings are present in the only application configuration file.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `server.shutdown: graceful` and an explicit shutdown phase timeout such as `spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase: 30s`. Tune the timeout to the deployment platform termination grace period.
